Article Title: 'Ballot paper, still we ask': Kharge dares BJP to dissolve Parliament after MLC poll setback
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday reiterated the opposition's demand for voting using ballot paper despite the party's lacklustre performance in the Karnataka MLC elections, which were held using ballot papers.Reacting to the Karnataka MLC results, Kharge said the opposition would not give up its demand for ballot paper voting simply because BJP won the elections. He also challenged the BJP to dissolve Parliament and contest elections using ballot papers."Ballot paper, still we ask. It doesn't mean that we should leave because they are winning. Once upon a time they won only two Parliament seats. Sometimes it happens, that doesn't mean that party has no hold," Kharge said."That ego should not be there in BJP that they have done very well. If that is the case, let them dissolve the Parliament and go on ballot paper," he added.Kharge's remarks came after Prime Minister Narendra Modi took a dig at Congress for "drawing a blank" in recent MLC elections. The grand old party had won zero seats till Wednesday night. The party, however, opened its account after retaining Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency seat."MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" PM Modi said in a post on X.BJP national president Nitin Nabin also targeted Congress, saying the party would continue to struggle for survival under Rahul Gandhi's leadership. Addressing a gathering during the BJP's ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ march in Delhi, Nabin said PM Narendra Modi would return to the Red Fort after the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.Nabin also accused Congress of opposing the revision of electoral rolls because it was distressed by efforts to remove alleged infiltrators.“There are voters who have died but whose names remain on the electoral rolls. There are also people whose names appear in the voter lists at two places. There are crores of such voters whose names are registered more than once, while the whereabouts of many others cannot be traced.This is what is called a ‘ghost voter list’,” he said.The remarks followed the BJP-JD(S) alliance's sweep of all four Karnataka legislative council seats, despite Congress being in power in the state. The results also saw Congress lose its sitting Bengaluru Teachers’ constituency to the JD(S), while the BJP retained three seats.PM Modi's reference to ballot papers comes amid the opposition's repeated allegations of irregularities in electronic voting machines (EVMs) and demands for greater transparency in the electoral process.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge says opposition will not give up its demand for ballot paper voting. He also challenged the BJP to dissolve Parliament and contest elections using ballot papers. Prime Minister Narendra Modi took a dig at Congress for "drawing a blank" in recent MLC elections.

Article Title: NDA wins 1 6 of 28 seats, Congress falters in MLC polls
Article Text:

PK’s party gets 1st council seat, ends CPI’s lone representation

BJP-led NDA won 16 of 28 seats in MLC polls held across four states, sweeping all four Karnataka legislative council constituencies, dealing a setback to Congress. Bihar and Maharashtra delivered split verdicts, while BJP led in UP as counting of paper ballots continued from Tuesday till late Wednesday.In Karnataka, JD(S) wrested Bengaluru teachers from Congress, while BJP won North East teachers, West graduates and South East graduates. D K Shivakumar, facing his first polls as CM, said Congress would take corrective measures. “We respect the verdict. We had expected two seats, but that did not happen,” he said.Congress had demanded a return to ballot papers.But results suggested its setbacks stemmed from organisational weaknesses. Party insiders said 19 ministers assigned to oversee 133 assembly segments failed to deliver, amid growing internal differences. BJP and JD(S) coordinated more closely than in previous polls.In Bihar, NDA won four of eight seats, while RJD and Prashant Kishor’s Jan Suraaj won one each. Independents took the remaining two. All four sitting teachers’ constituency MLCs lost, while incumbents retained all four graduates’ seats.RJD-backed Sanjeev Kumar defeated BJP veteran Nawal Yadav, a five-term MLC who had held Patna teachers for three decades. Jan Suraaj’s Suresh Prasad Rai defeated former Bihar Congress chief Madan Mohan Jha by 324 votes in Darbhanga teachers, giving Kishor’s party its first council seat and ending CPI’s lone representation.In UP, BJP won six seats and SP three among nine seats declared by Wednesday evening. Counting continued in Lucknow and Varanasi graduates’ constituencies. Independent Dhruv Tripathi, who later joined BJP, won Gorakhpur-Faizabad teachers for a fourth consecutive term, defeating Independent Rajiv Yadav by 307 votes.Maharashtra’s five MLC seats were closely contested between Mahayuti and opposition alliance MVA, with both winning two each. Among Mahayuti’s victories, BJP candidate Kaustubh Gawade won Pune teachers, while Sena’s Kiran Sarnaik took Amravati teachers.Sharad Pawar’s NCP-SP won two.In Nagpur, outcome remained uncertain after over 40 hours of counting, with BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale and Congress’s Abhijeet Wanjari trading leads through the day.State Congress chief Harshwardhan Sapkal said: “Our party contested three seats and made every effort to win. A large number of votes were declared invalid, which is a matter of concern.”
Article Summary: BJP-led NDA won 16 of 28 seats in MLC polls held across four states. Bihar and Maharashtra delivered split verdicts, while BJP led in UP. JD(S) wrested Bengaluru teachers from Congress. All four sitting teachers’ constituency MLCs lost. incumbents retained all four graduates’ seats.

Article Title: 'Commit to ballot paper': Congress dares PM Modi after his 'how many seats' swipe over MLC results

The grand old party which failed to win a single seat in the polls, hit back at PM Modi over his “ballot paper” remark and challenged him to commit to holding all future Lok Sabha and assembly elections using ballot papers.The back-and-forth began when the Prime Minister in a post on X, wrote, "MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?"Congress Rajya Sabha member Pawan Khera hit back at PM Modi, asking him to demonstrate confidence in the BJP’s prowess by committing to ballot paper voting in all future Lok Sabha and assembly elections.In a post on X, Khera demanded the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the restoration of 13.3 crore voters "deleted illegally"."If Narendra Modi is so confident that EVMs have no bearing on election results, let him prove his confidence in the BJP’s electoral prowess through action, not rhetoric," he wrote."1. Commit to conducting all Lok Sabha and upcoming Vidhan Sabha elections by ballot paper going forward.2. Suspend SIR and restore the 13.3 crore voters illegally deleted from the electoral rolls. 3. Addressing a gathering during the BJP's ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ march in Delhi, Nabin said PM Narendra Modi would return to the Red Fort after the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.Nabin also accused the Congress of opposing the cleaning of electoral rolls because it was distressed by efforts to remove alleged infiltrators.“There are voters who have died but whose names remain on the electoral rolls. There are also people whose names appear in the voter lists at two places. There are crores of such voters whose names are registered more than once, while the whereabouts of many others cannot be traced. This is what is called a ‘ghost voter list’,” he said.The remark came after the Congress drew a blank in Karnataka, where the BJP-Janata Dal (Secular) alliance swept all four legislative council seats despite the Congress being in power in the state. The results also saw the Congress lose its sitting Bengaluru Teachers’ constituency to the JD(S).The prime minister's reference to ballot papers comes amid the opposition's repeated allegations of irregularities in electronic voting machines (EVMs) and demands for greater transparency in the electoral process.The Congress suffered its biggest setback in Karnataka, where the BJP retained three seats and the JD(S) wrested Bengaluru Teachers’ from the ruling party.JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated sitting Congress MLC Puttanna by 908 votes, securing 10,810 votes against his rival's 9,902.The BJP retained the North-East Teachers’, South-East Graduates’ and West Graduates’ constituencies. The results came despite campaigning by chief minister Siddaramaiah, deputy chief minister D K Shivakumar and other senior Congress leaders.In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP won four of the 11 legislative council seats, while the Samajwadi Party secured two, with counting continuing in some constituencies.Bihar saw setbacks for both the Congress and the BJP. Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party opened its account in the state Legislative Council after candidate Suresh Prasad Rai defeated sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha by 324 votes in the Darbhanga Teachers’ constituency.

Article Title: Supreme Court says legality of EC's 'logical discrepancy' checks in SIR remains undecided
Article Text:
The clarification came during a hearing on a petition alleging a lack of transparency in notices.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What is the ‘logical discrepancy’ category

The Supreme Court on Wednesday clarified that it has not yet delivered a final ruling on the Election Commission of India ’s (ECI) use of the “logical discrepancy” category to flag voters’ details during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said its earlier decision allowing the Election Commission to use the category in West Bengal was only an interim measure. It also clarified that the court’s ruling on the SIR exercise in Bihar had not settled every legal question surrounding the revision process.The clarification came during a hearing on a petition alleging a lack of transparency in notices issued to voters during the ongoing SIR exercise in Delhi. Senior advocate D S Naidu, appearing for the Election Commission, had argued that the court had examined all stages of the SIR process and upheld its validity.Justice Bagchi rejected the suggestion that the earlier proceedings had conclusively settled the legality of the logical discrepancy category.“Bihar is not a final determination of every question arising in these proceedings. In Bihar, the Election Commission had not initially undertaken logical discrepancy as a category.We permitted it as an interim arrangement in West Bengal. We have not finally adjudicated upon the legality of the logical discrepancy exercise,” Justice Bagchi was quoted as saying by the news agency PTI.The judge also cautioned against treating oral observations made during hearings as final judicial decisions, particularly in sensitive cases."We do not wish to make further comments because observations in sensitive matters are sometimes taken out of context. These observations are not conclusive. There is a difficulty when judicial observations are repeatedly cited out of context as if every issue has already been decided," he said.During the SIR exercise, the Election Commission uses the “logical discrepancy” category to flag inconsistencies in voters’ records. These discrepancies are identified through ERONet, the poll panel’s centralised technology platform, which uses automated checks to examine electoral data.Such flags can arise when information in a voter’s profile or details linking family members appear inconsistent with mathematical, biological or clerical records. The category is intended to identify entries that require scrutiny.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday clarified that it has not yet delivered a final ruling on the Election Commission of India ’s use of the ‘logical discrepancy’ category. The clarification came during a hearing on a petition alleging a lack of transparency in notices issued to voters during the ongoing SIR exercise in Delhi.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Thursday questioned the PM Modi government over unemployment, inflation and private investment, saying voters delivered a “no-confidence motion” against its policies.In a post on X, Ramesh asked PM Modi to introspect instead of targeting the Congress, citing the BJP ’s electoral setbacks in Varanasi and Nagpur.“The Prime Minister needs to introspect, but instead, he's lecturing others! Crores of families are reeling from back-breaking inflation, the youth are unemployed, and private investment has ground to a halt. Drop the arrogance and reflect on these issues!” he added.Ramesh further claimed that voters in several cities had rejected the BJP-led government's policies. “From Varanasi and Nagpur to Lucknow, Prayagraj, and Patna, the people have clearly passed a no-confidence motion against your policies,” he added.The Congress leader’s remarks came a day after PM Modi took a swipe at the party over the National Democratic Alliance’s (NDA) performance in the legislative council elections across four states.In a post on X on October 28, PM Modi referred to elections held for 28 seats across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka, asking how many seats the Congress had won.The BJP won 13 of the 28 Legislative Council seats contested across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka, while the Samajwadi Party won five seats in Uttar Pradesh including Varanasi.In Karnataka, the BJP-led NDA swept all four seats, with the BJP winning three and the JD(S) wresting the Bengaluru Teachers’ seat from the Congress.In Maharashtra, the BJP won the Pune Teachers’ seat, the Shiv Sena won Amravati Teachers’, the Congress retained Nagpur Graduates’, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) faction won Pune Graduates’ and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Graduates’.In Bihar, the BJP won three of the eight seats, while the JD(U), RJD and Jan Suraaj Party won one each, and two went to Independents. RJD’s Sanjeev Kumar defeated BJP veteran Nawal Kishore Yadav in Patna Teachers’, JD(U)’s Neeraj Kumar retained Patna Graduates’, and Jan Suraaj’s Suresh Prasad Rai won Darbhanga Teachers’, giving the party its first seat in the Legislative Council.Independent candidates Rahul Raj and Banshidhar Brijvasi also won seats in Bihar.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned the PM Modi government over unemployment, inflation and private investment. He asked PM Modi to introspect instead of targeting the Congress. Article Title: Former TMC minister Indranil Sen arrested in Durga Puja pass scam case
Article Text:
Mamata Banerjee along with Indranil Sen

NEW DELHI: Former TMC minister Indranil Sen was arrested by Kolkata Police on Wednesday in connection with alleged financial irregularities involving Durga Puja preview shows and the sale of privileged-entry passes. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari alleged that former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee may also have benefited from the money collected in the alleged scam.Sen, a singer who held the tourism and culture portfolios in the previous Trinamool Congress government, was arrested after being questioned by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and Kolkata Police. The investigation concerns alleged irregularities by MassArt Society, with which Sen, his wife Madhuchhanda and their associates were allegedly associated.Reacting to the arrest, Adhikari said Sen and Banerjee shared a close association, often travelling and singing together. "It would be a mistake to think that Indranil Sen took the money alone. He must have shared it with Mamata Banerjee. She may also have had a share," he alleged.Adhikari also referred to their rendition of the popular Nazrul Sangeet 'Amar Jawar Samay' at a public programme last year. "I have heard their last song...It said, 'It is time for me to leave; bid me farewell'," he said, adding that "institutional thieves will have to go to jail".The chief minister alleged that Sen had received several lakhs of rupees from the state Information and Cultural Affairs Department through an event management company floated in his wife's name. He also accused Sen of taking money from envelopes meant for artistes and using the proceeds to construct a farmhouse in Singur. These allegations have not been established in court.The case originated from a complaint filed by Jaideep Mukherjee at Kolkata's Bowbazar police station. The ED subsequently launched a separate investigation.According to the allegations, MassArt Society collected money between 2022 and 2025 from people seeking privileged entry to Durga Puja celebrations, allegedly claiming to be a UNESCO-sponsored entity despite having no such commercial agreement with the organisation.The ED's preliminary estimate puts the alleged irregularities at Rs 50-60 crore.The society, established after Durga Puja received UNESCO intangible cultural heritage recognition in 2021, has Madhuchhanda Sen as its president, the agency said.Sen was questioned by ED officials for at least four hours at the agency's CGO Complex office in Salt Lake before Kolkata Police took him to its headquarters at Lalbazar.He had approached the Calcutta High Court for anticipatory bail, but his plea was rejected. He subsequently challenged the order in the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Indranil Sen was arrested by Kolkata Police on Wednesday in connection with alleged financial irregularities. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari alleged that former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee may also have benefited from the money collected in the alleged scam.

Article Title: 'Didn't want Mamata to contest another election': Suvendu Adhikari on why he kept Bhabanipur seat

NEW DELHI: Explaining his decision to vacate his Nandigram stronghold and retain Bhabanipur, West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Wednesday that vacating the Bhabanipur seat would have given his predecessor, Mamata Banerjee , another opportunity to contest the subsequent bypoll and return to the state assembly.Adhikari, who won both seats in the West Bengal assembly elections in April, defeated Mamata Banerjee in Bhabanipur. He had also defeated the then chief minister in Nandigram in the 2021 assembly elections, following which the TMC supremo contested a bypoll from Bhabanipur and won.The chief minister also took a dig at his predecessor, suggesting that she should retire from electoral politics given her age.“Had I vacated Bhabanipur, the person (Mamata Banerjee) I had defeated twice would have got another opportunity to contest an election. I did not want to give her that opportunity. I had trounced her in Bhabanipur, and I would urge her not to contest elections any more. You have already crossed 75 years of age. There is no need to enter the electoral fray any further. You should take rest at home,” PTI quoted Adhikari as saying.He made the remarks after Hasirani Rath and Shakharav Sarkar were sworn in as BJP MLAs following their victories in the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls earlier this month.The BJP leader also sought to reassure people in Nandigram, who he said were “upset” with him for leaving the constituency. He asserted that he would fulfil his commitments to them through Hasirani Rath, the newly elected MLA from Nandigram.“The people of Nandigram were upset with me for leaving the constituency, but I have explained my decision to them. I had to leave Nandigram for this reason. The people have now elected Hasirani Rath with a margin of 1.22 lakh votes. I will fulfil my promise to them through her,” he added.Hasirani Rath is the mother of Chandranath Rath, Adhikari’s aide who was shot dead on May 6, two days after the West Bengal assembly election results were declared. The BJP came to power in the state for the first time, ending the TMC’s 15-year rule.Turning to the murder of Chandranath Rath, Adhikari alleged that his aide was killed because of his association with him, describing it as a “supari”, or contract killing.“Chandranath was murdered simply because he was my aide. The CBI has arrested seven people, including the shooters and contract killers. What remains to be established is where the Rs 2 crore ‘supari’ for the contract killing came from. Was it Camac Street, Kalighat or Diamond Harbour? Once that is known, the investigation will be complete,” he said.Adhikari appeared to be referring to Camac Street, associated with the office of Trinamool Congress national general secretary and Mamata's nephew Abhishek Banerjee; Kalighat, where Mamata Banerjee resides; and Diamond Harbour, the Lok Sabha constituency represented by Abhishek Banerjee.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Wednesday that vacating the Bhabanipur seat would have given his predecessor, Mamata Banerjee, another opportunity to contest the subsequent bypoll. He made the remarks after Hasirani Rath and Shakharav Sarkar were sworn in as BJP MLAs following their victories in the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls.

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party BJP ) on Wednesday nominated senior leader and Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri for the Rajya Sabha bypoll in Madhya Pradesh.According to an official press release issued from the BJP's central office on Deen Dayal Upadhyay Marg, the party's Central Election Committee cleared Puri's name for the Upper House seat."The Central Election Committee of the Bharatiya Janata Party has given its approval to the name for the upcoming Rajya Sabha bye-election 2026 in Madhya Pradesh: Hardeep Singh Puri," the statement read.The bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of former Union minister L Murugan, who vacated the seat on October 14. His term in the Rajya Sabha was originally scheduled to end on April 2, 2030.The Election Commission announced the schedule for the bypoll on October 22.According to the schedule, the notification for the election will be issued on October 26. The last date for filing nominations is November 2, while scrutiny will take place on November 3. Candidates can withdraw their nominations until November 5.Polling will be held on November 12 from 9am to 4pm, followed by counting at 5pm on the same day. The entire election process is scheduled to be completed by November 16, the poll panel said.Puri, a former diplomat who later entered politics, currently serves as a Union Cabinet minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's government and holds the petroleum and natural gas portfolio.
Article Summary: Hardeep Singh Puri is a Union Cabinet minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government. The bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of former Union minister L Murugan, who vacated the seat on October 14. His term in the Rajya Sabha was originally scheduled to end on April 2, 2030.

Article Title: 'Failed to establish presence': BJP takes 'ballot paper' jibe at Rahul after Congress draws blank in MLC polls
Article Text:
BJP targets Rahul after MLC poll results, says Congress failed to make its presence felt

Karnataka: BJP-JD(S) sweep all four seats

Uttar Pradesh: BJP vs SP battle

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Wednesday targeted Congress over the results of MLC elections across four states, claiming that the grand old party has "failed to make its presence felt" in the polls conducted using ballot papers.The BJP's strong remarks came amid Congress leader Rahul Gandhi 's repeated allegations against the Election Commission and CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities.Addressing a presser, BJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi said, "The message is clear... the Congress party has failed to make its presence felt in these (MLC ) elections. More importantly, these elections were conducted using ballot boxes and ballot papers, yet the Congress failed to establish its presence. To put it in terms that the Congress leaders would understand better, the party has failed to make its very existence felt. This makes it clear that the Congress party lacks the ability to secure public support or the support of the voters concerned in any election, whether it is conducted using EVMs or ballot papers."BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi launched attack on Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi as the BJP and its NDA allies registered wins in the MLC elections.He said, "The Congress party should understand that Rahul Gandhi, after spending nearly two weeks sightseeing and enjoying himself, has now returned to the limelight and is talking about launching a movement that could create problems for the Indian economy. He must understand that neither the public nor the MLAs are with him. The Congress party must understand that public support is earned through hard work, not through sightseeing and leisure trips.""Our national president, Nitin Nabin, is travelling to Uttar Pradesh, while Amit Shah is in Punjab. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi had disappeared from the scene and was wandering around 'Champa'. 'Champa' was the ancient name of Vietnam. After that, he expects to receive public support. I would therefore like to tell the Congress party... give up your habit of avoiding hard work, and the slogan of 'vote theft' will automatically disappear," Sudhanshu Trivedi added.The BJP's remarks came as the party and its allies registered wins in several Legislative Council constituencies, while the Congress faced setbacks in Karnataka and Bihar.In Karnataka, the BJP took a jibe at chief minister DK Shivakumar after the opposition BJP-JD(S) alliance swept all four seats in the state's Legislative Council elections, leaving the ruling Congress without a win.The BJP's Karnataka unit posted on X, saying, "DK, it’s done, bro!"It added, "NDA SWEEPS 4/4 Teachers’ and Graduates’ constituencies in the MLC elections!"The BJP retained the North-East Teachers', South-East Graduates' and West Graduates' constituencies, while its ally JD(S) wrested the Bengaluru Teachers' seat from the Congress.In Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins in Varanasi and Agra, while the BJP secured three of the 11 Legislative Council seats, with counting under way in the remaining constituencies, officials said on Wednesday.SP supremo Akhilesh Yadav accused the BJP of resorting to alleged electoral malpractice to win the Uttar Pradesh MLC elections. He claimed that irregularities in the counting process had exposed a conspiracy to defeat SP candidate Sanjayan Tripathi.In a post on X, Akhilesh alleged that BJP leaders, their associates and officials had colluded to manipulate the counting process. He claimed that the alleged treatment of Tripathi had angered teachers and his community, and vowed that his party would oppose what he described as injustice and harassment.The BJP has denied no specific allegations in the information provided.In Bihar, the Prashant Kishor-led Jan Suraaj Party opened its account in the Legislative Council elections after its candidate Suresh Prasad Rai defeated sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha by 324 votes in the Darbhanga Teachers' constituency, officials said on Wednesday.BJP candidate Narendra Prasad Singh had on Tuesday defeated his nearest rival, Independent nominee Bhushan Kumar Jha, to win the Tirhut Teachers' constituency.Counting was still under way for some Legislative Council seats, officials said.
Article Summary: BJP targets Rahul after MLC poll results, says Congress failed to make its presence felt. BJP-JD(S) sweep all four seats in Karnataka. Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins in Varanasi and Agra. BJP secured three of the 11 Legislative Council seats.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Article Title: No UP govt jobs for those involved in violent activities seeking ‘regime change’
Article Text:
UP govt has clarified, however, that political ideology alone cannot be a ground for declaring a candidate ineligible for a government job.

(With inputs from PTI)

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with the decision to tighten character verification for government job candidates? Yes, it's necessary for public safety No, it limits political expression 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





LUCKNOW: The Uttar Pradesh government has revised its recruitment guidelines to make candidates associated with organisations advocating violent changes to the established system ineligible for state government jobs.The new rules also permanently bar candidates implicated in certain serious offences from government employment.The guidelines were issued on Wednesday by Principal Secretary (Appointment and Personnel) M Devaraj, following directives from the high court. They apply to all state government departments, public sector corporations, boards, and urban and rural local bodies.According to the circular, membership of an organisation that seeks to alter the “vidyaman vyavastha” (established system) through violent methods will make a candidate ineligible for government employment.The order, however, distinguishes between political beliefs and support for violence.“(One's) political ideology won't serve as a ground for disqualifying anyone from holding government jobs,” the order reads. It, however, adds that those “associated with organisations whose 'sankalpit uddeshya' or avowed purpose is to force a regime change through violent means will be considered ineligible.”The revised rules also permanently disqualify candidates implicated in serious offences, including murder, dacoity, rape, outraging modesty, corruption, acts of terror, recruitment examination paper leaks and organised “solver gang” rackets.The guidelines set out a three-year period for assessing a candidate’s involvement in activities related to violent changes to the established system.If an applicant has participated in such activities within three years before the verification date, after attaining 21 years of age, authorities will presume that the person remains actively involved.However, officials may consider documented evidence showing a genuine positive change in the candidate’s conduct and mindset during this period.The government has also clarified that a first information report (FIR) or an ongoing police investigation will not, by itself, lead to disqualification.Candidates who have been acquitted, resolved cases through lawful compromises, or whose cases fall under the Juvenile Justice Act will not face automatic rejection.Existing state government employees will not need fresh character verification. However, authorities may seek relevant service records from their previous parent departments.The new guidelines also seek to prevent delays in recruitment caused by pending verification reports. Appointment letters will not be withheld solely because character verification is incomplete.Appointing authorities may issue provisional appointment letters on the basis of a candidate’s self-declaration and prescribed undertakings. If any information is subsequently found to be false, the appointment will be cancelled and criminal proceedings initiated.Under the revised procedure, district police and the Local Intelligence Unit (LIU) must submit character verification reports within 30 days of receiving a request. The state home department will directly monitor compliance with the deadline.The guidelines also place restrictions on verification procedures to prevent harassment of applicants. Police and intelligence officials have been instructed not to visit candidates’ homes for questioning, and applicants will not be required to appear physically at police stations.If a verification report is adverse, the district magistrate must give the candidate an opportunity to present their side, either in person or online, before forwarding a final adverse recommendation, the order said.
Article Summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has revised its recruitment guidelines to make candidates associated with organisations advocating violent changes ineligible for state government jobs. The new rules also permanently bar candidates implicated in certain serious offences from government employment. The guidelines were issued on Wednesday by Principal Secretary (Appointment and Personnel) M Devaraj, following directives from the high court.

Article Title: Woman tries to hurl purse at Bombay high court judge after eviction order goes against her
Article Text:
The Bombay HC deemed her actions as contempt of court during the contempt petition proceedings.





MUMBAI: Bombay high court came down heavily on a litigant who tried to throw her purse at a judge after an order was passed against her and her three children.“Minder Gurmit Singh Thukral has behaved in a wholly inappropriate manner, which also amounts to contempt of court,” justice Madhav Jamdar noted in Tuesday’s order.HC was hearing a contempt petition against the Thukrals. An eviction decree in a 2009 suit filed by the landlord against Thukral’s father-in-law was executed in April 2025. Thereafter the Thukrals re-entered the property. The landlord’s family moved HC.Justice Jamdar said, “prima facie, I am satisfied that the conduct of the respondents amounts to interference in the administration of justice.”He appointed the court receiver to take symbolic possession of the premises by Wednesday and remain present on Thursday for handover of possession to the petitioners.Further, if possession is not handed over, the court receiver shall take physical possession and immediately hand it over to the landlord. HC permitted taking police protection.It was then that Thukral started crying and shouting. She tried to throw her purse at the judge but stopped herself. She submitted a written apology.But Justice Jamdar questioned her conduct, saying, “just because an order is passed against you, doesn’t mean you will behave in such a manner.”He summoned the police, who removed Thukral from the courtroom. Justice Jamdar indicated imposing heavy costs and initiating contempt proceedings against her. He posted the hearing regarding “conduct of all the respondents and also conduct of” Thukral on Oct 30.
Article Summary: HC was hearing a contempt petition against the Thukrals. An eviction decree in a 2009 suit filed by the landlord against Thukral’s father-in-law was executed in April 2025. The landlord's family moved HC. HC permitted taking police protection.

Article Title: UP MLC polls: SP secures Varanasi and Agra seat, BJP wins 4
Article Text:
Lal Bihari Yadav secured the Varanasi Teachers' seat





LUCKNOW: BJP retained four Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats, including both constituencies in Meerut, the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ seat and the Lucknow Teachers’ seat, while the Samajwadi Party secured victories in the Varanasi and Agra Teachers’ constituencies as counting for 11 MLC seats continued.In the Meerut-Saharanpur Graduates’ constituency, BJP’s sitting MLC Dinesh Goyal retained his seat, defeating SP candidate Pramod Singh Bhati by 12,855 votes. BJP’s Shrichand Sharma also retained the Meerut Teachers’ constituency, defeating SP candidate Nitin Tomar by 13,241 votes.BJP’s Hari Singh Dhillon retained the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ constituency, defeating SP candidate Haji Mohammad Danish Akhtar.In another victory for the BJP, sitting MLC Umesh Dwivedi retained the Lucknow Teachers’ constituency, defeating SP candidate Sushil Kumar (Baba). UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary congratulated Dwivedi on his victory in a post on X on Wednesday morning, expressing confidence that he would continue working for the development of the education sector.Meanwhile, SP’s sitting MLC Lal Bihari Yadav retained the Varanasi Teachers’ constituency, defeating BJP candidate Pramod Mishra by approximately 4,900 votes.In the Agra Teachers’ constituency, SP candidate Akash Agrawal emerged victorious, defeating BJP candidate Hari Kishore Tiwari. Agrawal had won the same seat as an Independent in 2020. His latest victory means he has retained the constituency, this time as an SP candidate.In the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ constituency, BJP’s Dhruv Tripathi was leading by a narrow margin of 110 votes in the last available update, with Independent candidate Rajeev Yadav and SP candidate Sanjayan also in contention.Polling for five Graduates’ and six Teachers’ constituencies was held on October 23, with 152 candidates in the fray. Repolling at three polling stations in the Agra Teachers’ constituency took place on Monday following orders from the Election Commission.Final results from the remaining constituencies were awaited.
Article Summary: BJP retained four Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats, including both constituencies in Meerut, the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ seat and the Lucknow Teachers' seat. Samajwadi Party secured victories in the Varanasi and Agra Teachers' constituencies.

Article Title: 'Ballot' jolt for Congress: BJP-JD(S) sweeps all 4 Karnataka MLC seats
Article Text:
Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar

Rifts within Congress in focus

19 ministers on poll job, Cong gets 0





BENGALURU: The BJP-JD(S) NDA swept all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats in polls held through ballot papers, dealing a blow to governing Congress ahead of the 2028 assembly polls. DK Shivakumar , facing his first polls since taking over as chief minister, said Congress would take corrective measures in view of these results. "We respect the verdict. We had expected to win two seats, but that did not happen. The Bengaluru Teachers' result, particularly, was unexpected. We will review it. Although we lost, we secured a good number of votes," Shivakumar said.Opposition BJP mocked Shivakumar after the outcome as Congress has been demanding a switch from EVMs to ballot papers. "DK, it's done, bro! NDA sweeps all four Teachers' and Graduates' constituencies in the MLC elections," the party posted on X."MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states -- Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" PM Modi said on X. It was an apparent taunt at Congress's continuing troubles and a rebuke to the opposition party's claim that BJP's successes are because of the EVMs and electoral rolls.The polls covered 19 districts, comprising nearly two-thirds of the state, including the home districts of former CM Siddaramaiah and AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge. JD(S) candidate AP Ranganath wrested Bengaluru Teachers' seat from Congress, defeating sitting MLC Puttanna by 908 votes, while BJP won the other three seats.In North East Teachers' seat, Shashil G Namoshi beat Sharanappa Mattur by 3,297 votes. In West Graduates' constituency, SV Sankanur posted a hat-trick of wins, beating Congress's Mohan Limbikai by 9,323, while in South East Graduates' seat, KM Suresh trounced Shashi Hulikuntemath by 23,098 votes.KPCC president BK Hariprasad, who was also facing his first test at the hustings since his appointment, said the party will conduct a comprehensive review of its organisational and political shortcomings.Multiple factors are said to have dealt a blow to Congress. According to party insiders, Shivakumar, despite himself being a master poll strategist, had assigned 19 ministers to oversee 133 assembly segments under the four constituencies that went to the polls, while he himself was busy with protests over SIR, Dasara preparations and his political trips to Delhi.The failure of ministers to deliver the goods is being seen by some political functionaries as a reflection of growing differences within the party since Shivakumar became CM. Teachers' resentment over govt's failure to restore the old pension scheme may have cost Congress both the teachers' seats.On the other hand, BJP and JD(S) showed better coordination this time around than in previous polls. In Bengaluru, BJP functionaries consolidated their party's votes behind Ranganath.
Article Summary: BJP-JD(S) NDA swept all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats in polls held through ballot papers. DK Shivakumar facing his first polls since taking over as chief minister, said Congress would take corrective measures. "We respect the verdict. We had expected to win two seats, but that did not happen," he said.

Article Title: Lawyers’ Body Calls Off Strike After Cops Are Transferred
Article Text: New Delhi: The Coordination Committee of All District Court Bar Associations of Delhi called off its indefinite strike in Delhi’s lower courts following the transfer of two police officers for allegedly assaulting lawyers at Shahdara police station on Oct 23.Following a meeting between the lawyers and Delhi Police , an ACP was moved to the Special Police Unit for Women and Children (SPUWAC), while an SHO was transferred to the security unit.Advocate Neeraj, chairperson of the coordination committee, expressed his gratitude to the legal fraternity for “their unwavering support, solidarity and collective resolve.”Dhir Singh Kasana, former secretary-general of the Saket Court bar association, added: “Both the implicated officers have been transferred following our protest, and now the judicial work will resume from tomorrow.”However, the lawyers reiterated their other demands, including completion of an inquiry into complaints lodged by the Shahdara Bar Association against the erring police officers within two months.The committee also demanded immediate and effective steps to apprehend the accused, named in FIR 248/2026, at Shahdara police station, warning that lawyers would pursue legal steps. It also demanded that the investigation into the FIR against advocates at Shahdara police station be completed in a week.
Article Summary: The Coordination Committee of All District Court Bar Associations of Delhi called off its indefinite strike in Delhi’s lower courts following the transfer of two police officers for allegedly assaulting lawyers at Shahdara police station. An ACP was moved to the Special Police Unit for Women and Children (SPUWAC), while an SHO was transferred to the security unit.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: TMC suspends fire chief over immersion ghats lapses
Article Text:
Thane municipal corporation





THANE: The Thane municipal corporation (TMC) on Friday suspended its acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence in providing adequate safety equipment at idol immersion ghats on Oct 20. Action has also been taken against two other officials, while show-cause notices have been served on two junior staff, it is learnt.The suspension order is issued by additional municipal commissioner-1, Prashant Rode, holds Jhalke responsible for lapses in carrying out his duties. The order states that he has been suspended under the Maharashtra Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1979. Jhalke, who is the fire officer and in-charge of Balkum fire station, has been handling the additional charge of CFO for the last several years."Certain safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake were allegedly found to be inadequate, with a particular shortfall in life jackets and other essential safety equipment. The shortcomings were apparently pointed out to deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde who also expressed concern at the alleged negligence," said a civic official.Officials said that during the suspension period, Jhalke will be required to comply with the prescribed conditions and cannot take up other employment or engage in business without the requisite permission.
Article Summary: Thane municipal corporation suspends acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence. Action also taken against two other officials, while show- cause notices have been served on two junior staff. Safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake allegedly found to be inadequate.

Article Title: Sealed Thane flat in Iqbal Kaskar-Dawood Ibrahim money laundering case breached; ED reclaims property, files FIR
Article Text:
Thane flat linked to Iqbal Kaskar’s extortion case targeted for occupation





MUMBAI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane which was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim The flat was attached in the case in 2022, in the money laundering case linked to extortion by Iqbal Kaskar and others.The flat was in ED’s possession and it had put its seal on the lock. Kaskar had acquired the flat through extortion and threat in 2015 and got it registered in the name of his associate Mumtaz Azaz Sheikh, alias Raju.Recently, the ED learnt that certain persons entered the flat after removing its possession notice, claiming ownership of the flat.Since the money laundering case is pending in the court, the ED informed the court about it, repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.
Article Summary: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane. The flat was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim. The ED repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.

Article Title: Maharashtra MLC polls: Congress candidate Abhijit Wanjarri wins Nagpur graduates' constituency with 67,231 votes
Article Text:
Abhijit Wanjarri, a Congress candidate, emerged victorious in the Nagpur Division Legislative Council elections.





NAGPUR: Congress candidate Abhijit Wanjarri has won the Nagpur Division Legislative Council Graduates’ Constituency election, securing a total of 67,231 votes after the first- and second-preference counts. His nearest rival, BJP candidate Sudhakar Kohale, received 63,960 votes.Election Returning Officer and Divisional Commissioner Vijayalakshmi Bidari handed over the certificate of election to Wanjarri.Vote counting began at 8am on Tuesday, October 27, at the Divisional Sports Complex in Mankapur, Nagpur, using 84 tables. The counting process continued for more than 41 hours. Election Observer Dr Harshdeep Kamble, Returning Officer and Divisional Commissioner Vijayalakshmi Bidari, assistant returning officers, collectors from all districts in the division, and officials and staff deployed for the counting were present.Neither candidate secured the required quota of 75,438 votes in the two rounds of first-preference counting. Consequently, a second-preference elimination round was conducted in accordance with the election procedure. Of the 1,65,906 votes counted in the two first-preference rounds, 15,032 were declared invalid, while 1,50,874 were found to be valid.No candidate secured the prescribed quota even after the second-preference elimination round.Therefore, Wanjarri, who secured the highest total of 67,231 votes across the first- and second-preference elimination rounds, was declared elected.The Election Commission of India announced the schedule for the Nagpur Division Legislative Council Graduates’ Constituency election on September 22. The election notification was issued on September 29. Polling was held on October 23 from 8am to 4pm. Vote counting began at 8am on October 27 and concluded after more than 41 hours. The Commission has scheduled October 31 as the deadline for completing the entire election process.
Article Summary: Congress candidate Abhijit Wanjarri has won the Nagpur Division Legislative Council Graduates’ Constituency election. His nearest rival, BJP candidate Sudhakar Kohale, received 63,960 votes. Vote counting began at 8am on Tuesday, October 27, at the Divisional Sports Complex in Mankapur, Nagpur.

Article Title: Properties of former TN minister Anbil Mahesh should be seized, BJP leader demands
Article Text:
Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi





COIMBATORE: BJP state general secretary A P Muruganandam has demanded a thorough probe into an alleged Rs 100crore corruption case involving former Tamil Nadu school education minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi and called for the seizure of assets accumulated in the names of Mahesh and his alleged benamis.In a statement on Tuesday, Muruganandam alleged that corruption in the school education department had brought disrepute to the state. He said it involved issuing new licences and renewing recognition for private schools in exchange of bribes.Muruganandam said private schools should meet safety and infrastructure norms, including structurally sound buildings, fire safety measures, proper ventilation and playground facilities. He alleged that approvals were granted to ineligible schools for bribes, risking the safety of students.He added that private schools passed on bribery costs to parents through fees and other charges. He called the alleged Rs 100 crore corruption exploitation of poor and middle-class families. He asked whether such a large-scale scam could have occurred without the knowledge or involvement of senior political leaders, IAS officers and intermediaries.Muruganandam sought referral of the case to the Enforcement Directorate and other central agencies to investigate the alleged movement of illegal funds.
Article Summary: BJP state general secretary A P Muruganandam has demanded a thorough probe into an alleged Rs 100crore corruption case. He called for the seizure of assets accumulated in the names of Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi and his alleged benamis.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Woman hacked to death, gold chain snatched in Tuticorin
Article Text: Tuticorin: A 45-year-old woman was hacked to death allegedly by her 29-year-old nephew who entered her house on Wednesday afternoon and escaped with her four-sovereign gold thali chain.Police identified the deceased as C Sasikala, wife of Chithiraivel, a native of Third Mile area. Chithiraivel has been working in Kerala, while Sasikala was living alone at the house. Their married son lives separately and their daughter resides in Chennai.According to police, the incident occurred around 2.30 pm when the man, K Vignesh, entered the house and attacked Sasikala with a sickle, inflicting multiple cut injuries. He then fled with her thali chain.Thenpagam police rushed to the spot and sent the body to Tuticorin Govt Medical College Hospital for postmortem examination. Police launched an investigation and secured Vignesh. Initial investigation suggested that it was a murder for gain.
Article Summary: Police identified the deceased as C Sasikala, wife of Chithiraivel, a native of Third Mile area. Their married son lives separately and their daughter resides in Chennai. Police launched an investigation and secured Vignesh. Initial investigation suggested that it was a murder for gain.

Article Title: Sub-inspector suspended for bid to make minor girl retract Pocso complaint against her father
Article Text: MADURAI: A police sub-inspector in Ramanathapuram district tried to pressure a minor girl into withdrawing a Pocso complaint against her father, asking her to deny the sexual abuse allegations to help him secure bail.Following an inquiry, superintendent of police G Chandeesh has ordered the SI’s suspension.The girl’s father was arrested last month under Pocso Act for allegedly sexually abusing her.He was subsequently remanded to judicial custody.A senior police officer said the uncle of the accused was attempting to secure his release on bail when he approached Asaikumar, a sub-inspector attached to the Thondi police station who was handling court-related duties. “Asaikumar demanded and accepted a bribe, promising to help secure bail if the relative followed his instructions,” said the officer.The girl’s family approached the SP with an audio recording of the SI allegedly instructing the uncle of the accused to make the girl claim that she had made a false allegation and no sexual abuse had taken place. The complaint prompted a departmental inquiry which substantiated the allegations against the SI.
Article Summary: The girl’s father was arrested last month under Pocso Act for allegedly sexually abusing her. He was subsequently remanded to judicial custody. The uncle of the accused was attempting to secure his release on bail when he approached Asaikumar, a sub-inspector attached to the Thondi police station.

Article Title: Husband slashes wife outside court during divorce hearing in Kanyakumari district
Article Text:
Madurai:





A woman appearing for a divorce hearing was critically injured after her estranged husband attacked her with a sickle outside the Padmanabhapuram family court in Kanyakumari district on Tuesday.Jerlin Prema, 32, was walking towards the court with her younger brother, Jerin, when Vincent Raj, a mason from Eethavilai near Thuckalay, intercepted her near the entrance and repeatedly slashed her with a concealed sickle.Lawyers who intervened were threatened with the weapon. Raj fled, but advocates and members of the public chased him for about 150m, caught him on Palace Road and handed him over to Thuckalay police.Prema, who suffered injuries to her head and limbs, was taken to Thuckalay govt hospital before being referred to Government Medical College Hospital in Asaripallam, where she was admitted for intensive treatment. Later, she was moved to a private hospital.Prema, who worked at a shop, married Raj about eight years ago. The couple have a son. Following marital disputes, she moved to her parents’ home in Ponmanai and filed for divorce. Police sources alleged that Raj had frequently assaulted her.Police registered a case of attempted murder and arrested Raj. Investigators said other criminal cases were pending against him.
Article Summary: Jerlin Prema, 32, was walking towards the court with her younger brother, Jerin. Vincent Raj, a mason from Eethavilai near Thuckalay, intercepted her near the entrance and repeatedly slashed her with a concealed sickle.

Article Title: PE teacher suspended after national flag turns upside down at state sports meet in Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions held at the Mahatma Gandhi Sports Ground here on Wednesday.The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag, and a snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down. The event was organized by the state school education department.Taking immediate note of the negligence during the flag-hoisting ceremony, Salem chief educational officer A Ellappan issued an order placing physical education teacher John Jamindar who had supervised the flag hoisting area.
Article Summary: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions. The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag. A snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down.

Article Title: Two history-sheeters who escaped from Attayampatti police station nabbed
Article Text: SALEM: Two history-sheeters, who escaped from the Attayampatti police station in Salem district on Tuesday, were nabbed in the early hours of Wednesday.The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. According to police, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu were brought to the Attayampatti police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub-inspector Krishnan and other police personnel. Subsequently, cases were registered against them.Later, police were making arrangements to produce them before a court in the evening. “However, taking advantage of an opportunity, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu managed to escape from the police station,” said a police officer.Special police teams were formed to trace them. After an intensive search operation, the duo were tracked down and arrested from near Tiruchengode around 3am on Wednesday.They were brought back to the Attayampatti police station for further inquiry. Later, they were lodged in the Salem Central Prison under judicial custody.
Article Summary: The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. They were brought to the police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub- inspector Krishnan and other police personnel.

Article Title: Woman robbed of gold ornaments after chilli water attack in Vennala
Article Text:
Kochi

:





An 82-year-old woman was robbed of gold ornaments worth Rs 2.38 lakh after a woman allegedly broke into her house and threw chilli water at her face in Vennala on Wednesday morning.The incident occurred around 9.25am at the rented house of Ponnamma on Kaniyappilly Road. The accused allegedly threatened to kill Ponnamma if she raised an alarm before snatching part of a gold chain weighing 2.25 sovereigns, including its locket, and a gold bangle weighing one sovereign from her right hand.Palarivattom Police registered a case based on a complaint lodged by Ponnamma’s son and launched an investigation.
Article Summary: The incident occurred around 9.25am at the rented house of Ponnamma on Kaniyappilly Road. She was robbed of a gold chain weighing 2.25 sovereigns, including its locket, and a gold bangle weighing one sovereign from her right hand. Palarivattom Police registered a case and launched an investigation.

Article Title: Madrassa teacher arrested in Pocso case at Ernakulam
Article Text:
Kochi:

Man held for stealing:

Police help accident victim recover lost anklet:





A 41-year-old madrassa teacher was arrested by Kalamassery police on Wednesday for allegedly sexually abusing a nine-year-old girl in Vattekkunnam, Ernakulam.According to the complaint, the accused, Abdul Aziz , of Payyanad, Palakkad, allegedly abused the girl multiple times during study hours at the madrassa.The arrest was made in Palakkad on Wednesday by a police team led by Kalamassery inspector AAL Abhilash.The case was registered at the Kalamassery police station under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act. The accused was produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody.Kalamassery police arrested a 26-year-old man for allegedly stealing copper wires and other household materials worth around Rs 65,000, which had been stored for the construction of a house belonging to a Kalamassery native.The accused, Rahul Ameen, hails from Assam’s Barpeta. The stolen items included copper wires, door handles, locks, pipe sets and other materials required for house construction.The accused was produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody. Police said he was involved in several other theft cases.Aluva police personnel came to the rescue of a woman injured in a road accident near Aluva govt hospital on Wednesday morning and later recovered her lost anklet.The woman, a native of Thuruth in Aluva, was riding a scooter around 9.30am when a car hit her, leaving her injured.Sub-inspector Kabeer K Ismail and civil police officer Ameen A Razak, who were travelling in an Aluva police control room vehicle, rushed her to the hospital.At the hospital, the woman told the police that she lost an anklet weighing around one-and-a-half sovereigns. The officers returned to the accident spot, searched the surrounding area and recovered the anklet lying on the road.They later returned to the hospital and handed over the anklet to the woman.
Article Summary: A 41-year-old madrassa teacher was arrested by Kalamassery police on Wednesday for allegedly sexually abusing a nine-year old girl. The accused, Abdul Aziz, of Payyanad, Palakkad, allegedly abused the girl multiple times during study hours at the madrassinga. Police help accident victim recover lost anklet.

Article Title: CBI court to pronounce verdict on Abdul Shukkoor murder case on Nov 12
Article Text:
Abdul Shukkoor

Kochi

:





A CBI special court on Wednesday reserved its verdict on the murder trial of IUML worker Abdul Shukkoor for Nov 12. CPM senior functionaries P Jayarajan and T V Rajesh are among the accused in the case.The court had declined to quash the trial proceedings against CPM former Kannur district secretary Jayarajan and former MLA and then DYFI state secretary Rajesh. Of the total 33 accused, two have since died.Shukkoor, 21, a native of Ariyil near Taliparamba, was murdered at Keezhara on Feb 20, 2012. The prosecution case is that the murder was in retaliation for an alleged attack by IUML workers on Jayarajan and Rajesh’s convoy during their visit to the tension-hit Ariyil area earlier that day.According to police, Shukkoor and four other youths had taken shelter in a house at Keezhara. A group of CPM workers allegedly intimidated the house owners, forcing the youths to leave. The assailants then photographed them on mobile phones and verified their identities with party workers. Three were released after the purported verification, while Shukkoor and another IUML worker, Zakaria, were taken to a nearby field and stabbed.Shukkoor died of his injuries, while Zakaria managed to escape.Jayarajan and Rajesh were charged under Section 118 of the Indian Penal Code after investigators allegedly found that they had prior knowledge of the conspiracy to murder Shukkoor. The conspiracy was allegedly hatched in a room at Taliparamba Co-operative Hospital, where the two senior functionaries had been admitted on Feb 20 after the alleged attack by IUML workers earlier that day.The investigation came under scrutiny following a petition by Shukkoor’s mother A C Aathikka. In 2016, Kerala High Court ordered a CBI investigation while allowing her writ petition. She contended that the police had failed to gather evidence concerning the alleged criminal conspiracy involving Jayarajan and Rajesh, whom she claimed had played an instrumental role in the murder.The petitioner also questioned the difference in the charges against the two senior functionaries and the other accused. While the remaining accused had been charged under Section 123(b) of the IPC in connection with the conspiracy, Jayarajan and Rajesh were charged under Section 118, which deals with concealing a design to commit an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
Article Summary: Abdul Shukkoor, 21, a native of Ariyil near Taliparamba, was murdered at Keezhara on Feb 20, 2012. CPM senior functionaries P Jayarajan and T V Rajesh are among the accused in the case. Of the total 33 accused, two have since died.
